name: Mere
title: One of King Ahasuerus' seven advisors
summary: Mere was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had direct access to King Ahasuerus (Xerxes). These seven wise men were the king's closest advisors and knew the law and justice. They were consulted when King Ahasuerus sought advice on how to handle Queen Vashti's disobedience.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the king's seven advisors
keyEvents.description: Mere is mentioned as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who sat closest to the king and held the highest rank in the kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Advice regarding Queen Vashti's disobedience
keyEvents.description: King Ahasuerus consulted with his seven wise men, including Memucan, when Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command during his great banquet.

keyEvents.title: The context of the advice – the king's banquet
keyEvents.description: During a great banquet that lasted for many days, the drunken king sent for Queen Vashti to display her beauty, but she refused to come.

keyEvents.title: Memucan's advice is followed
keyEvents.description: After consulting with the seven princes, including Memucan, it was Memucan who spoke and proposed that Vashti be stripped of her royal position. The king and the princes followed this advice.
